utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's almost time for another Status Conference, and I thought it may be appropriate -- I'm sorry I haven't given you warning, but when I looked up the dates, I realised the timing -- it may be appropriate to treat this as a Status Conference. If there is anything that you want to raise, either party, later on which you would have raised at a Status Conference, I will, of course, reconstitute it for that purpose. The only thing that is outstanding from the previous one is this troublesome matter of the exculpatory material, Rule 68. Ms. Kuo has been telling me how valiantly the Prosecution has been searching for this material each time. I think the time has come when we have some sort of a time limit on it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, having recently taken over conduct of this matter, I'm going to ask my colleague, Ms. Kuo, to deal with the issue of the exculpatory material. I understand that a number of materials have, in fact, been gathered, but I will let Ms. Kuo elaborate upon that to satisfy the Court's enquiry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We anticipate that within two month's time, we should have the exculpatory materials. We should be able to go through the materials we currently have and turn over any exculpatory materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's anything within your possession or within your knowledge, which would include material not only within your possession but material you know about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There had been a number of problems in trials recently with the compliance with this Rule, and I think that the time has come where we have to put some form of additional onus on the Prosecution. What I had in mind would be like an affidavit of discovery, which those of us who are familiar with the common law system would be very aware of. Perhaps the case manager should be able to take the responsibility for saying that there has been a complete search of all that material. I think there has come, myself, a time for this sort of procedure to be followed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: We would certainly be able to comply with that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Two months, you say?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's a Sunday. I think if we make it Monday, the 15th of November, would that be all right?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: That's agreeable, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry. Is there anything you want to say about this, Mr. Vasic? It's all in your favour, I would think, what I'm proposing, or in your client's favour, should I say. Is there anything you want to say about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. We understand that this is favourable to the Defence, and the more comprehensive material we receive, the better we will be able to prepare our defence. We are now expecting the materials from the Prosecution. I was even told that today I would be receiving further supporting materials. Based on what we receive, we will proceed as needed. The Defence will submit all the preliminary motions in as short a period of time as possible. As my client has pointed out, 15 months later, we have a further initial appearance, so we are at the starting point, but I want to thank Your Honour for considering the interests of the Defence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I know it's of no comfort to your client when I say this, but his trial is not in any way delayed by the need for the Prosecution to re-plead the indictment and for your client to re-plead. He is still the next trial but one in Trial Chamber II, but hopefully we'll have some better news for him about when his trial is due to start by the end of the year. I propose to make these orders. I'll hear what you want to say about the terms of them after I have set them out, and I'll make the order in these terms if there is no objection taken to them. "1. The prosecution is to comply, on or before the 15th of November, with its obligation pursuant to Rule 68 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence to disclose to the defence the existence of evidence known to it: (a) which may in any way tend to suggest the innocence of, or to mitigate the guilt of, the accused, or (b) which may affect the credibility of the prosecution evidence. The expression 'evidence' is intended to include any material which may put the accused on notice that material exists which may assist him in his defence, and it is not limited to material which is itself admissible in evidence. 2. On or before that date, the prosecution is to file an affidavit of its case manager for this case, sworn in accordance with the law and procedure of the State in which such affidavit is signed, in which he or she testifies: (a) that a full search has been conducted throughout the materials in the possession of the prosecution or otherwise within its knowledge for the existence of such evidence; and (b) that he or she is aware of the continuing nature of the obligation pursuant to Rule 68." Is there anything you want to say about those terms? Yes, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only thing is whether it needs to be the case manager. Our analyst on the team is the one that's been most intimately involved in this, and would it be more appropriate, perhaps, for that person to sign an affidavit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. I had suggested the case manager earlier only because I thought he or she, as the case may be, at any particular time would have the best knowledge. The analyst is what, a legal officer?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'm not sure exactly the technical status, but it's the person who has been working -- she has a law degree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is she employed as a P-2, or whatever, that's what I'm really after, as a legal officer?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I believe so. I don't know the exact -- I know it's a professional level, but I don't know the exact title.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: "Professional level" will do. The analyst; all right. Is that a sufficient description of the position, "analyst"? Analyst for this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, by substituting the word "analyst" for "case manager," I make orders in those terms. Is there anything else that either party wants to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If I may, if it please Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ryneveld.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: The manner of swearing of the affidavit requires clarification, of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I follow the terms of the Rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There is a rule relating to affidavits, and that is the terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So if it's signed here in the Netherlands, then somebody will have to find out how you swear an affidavit in the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you. The second issue, of course, is that my understanding is that the obligation for providing exculpatory material is an ongoing obligation, and I take it that if, as of the 15th of November, the affidavit indicates that all of the information then known to the Prosecution would be captured in that affidavit, if, of course, additional information became available thereafter, we would be on a continuing obligation to provide that to the Defence as quickly as it became known to us. Certainly there is a rule there as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: I just want to make absolutely sure that we understand that our obligation is an ongoing obligation and that the affidavit simply captures the information known to the Prosecution up to the date of the swearing of the affidavit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's so, but there is an ongoing obligation to disclose anything else that comes to the knowledge or into the possession of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. That's the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And it continues right up to the judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: And perhaps, arguably, even thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Oh, dear, yes, I suppose it does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But thank you for that. Is there anything that you want to raise, Mr. Vasic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour. I believe that this deadline of two months, since we have a new lead Prosecutor, is a necessary one, and we believe that we will receive all the pertinent materials within that period of time that we are supposed to be getting from the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. All right. If there is nothing else, I'll note that this has been a Status Conference and that the time limit imposed by the Rules for the next Status Conference will run from today. I'm grateful to counsel and to the parties generally for their assistance, and I'll adjourn.
